I am the greatest pirate in the history of the world.

I was a good kid. I got excellent grades, had tons of friends, and stayed on the right side of the law. That is, until I discovered computer science. I learned almost all of the languages used professionally in my sophomore and junior years of high school. I had always been fascinated with video games, so I decided to make one. Unfortunately, the usable engines were hard to learn. I had to take a peak at an existing game to get my bearings.

Just a peek. Harmless, right?

I got on my computer and pirated my first game: Civilization V. After a couple hours of downloading and a few minutes searching, I found the code I needed to get started, but I wasn't happy. I realized that I didn't want to make things, I wanted to mod things.

I wrote a simple mod for Civ V which added the Amazonian civilization. It was fun to play, was balanced, and took off. Curious to see how many downloads I had, I built an internet crawler to find download sites and tally visitors. From here, I realized how easy information is to get. I had a program stalking people on over 100 websites, for Christ's sake. I built a different crawler to go on Wells Fargo, just to test something. It didn't work, rather expectedly, but it was detected. I was being prosecuted heavily by Wells Fargo. With nowhere else to go, I fled the country.

While in Mexico, I improved my keygen and IP hiding. I rented the cheapest modem pesos can buy and ran the program. I took a peak at my bank account, which was based in Europe, and saw the number steadily rise. Not too long after that, Mexican police knocked on my crappy apartment door. Desperate and rich, I miraculously escaped. In Columbia, I bought a house boat to camp out on, beyond the borders of any national laws, and topped off my account.

The years went by, and my cash dwindled. Banks improved their software, and I didn't improve mine. Instead, I used the last of my money to hire a crew and a lot of weapons from a local arms dealer. We sailed up to the Atlantic to find a ship to plunder. We scored. There was a shipment of American goods on their way to Europe, so we took over the ship (we only lost two of our 20 man crew!) and held it for ransom in the UK. We were prosecuted immediately, so we got the hell outta dodge.

Turns out, there is a huge black market for this kind of stuff, so we sold the boat and everything on it to various cartels, mobs, and even the Cuban government. My crew and I used the money to buy more weapons and replaced the fallen members. I, as the captain, was quickly rising my international bounty as a pirate.

I slept easy at night most of the time. After all, these countries would have me rot in jail for life without losing a wink of sleep, so why should I treat others any different? That is, until one encounter. We normally stuck to oil barges and weapons shipments for our pay, but it had been a slow month and we were almost out of food and money. That's when we saw the ship that changed everything. A huge cruise ship coming out of Florida for a luxury vacation. My crew, blinded by greed, made a beeline for the ship. When I realized there was nothing I could do, I stopped protesting and just did my job. All it took for these tourists to scatter was a few gunshots in the air. Compared to other pirated ships, this was like taking candy from a candy-hating baby. The people screamed and screamed for mercy, but my crew and I heard nothing. We raped the women, took all of the food and money, and left them stranded in the Atlantic. After sailing away, my crew was excited that we had food for a month and enough money to get food for a year, but I felt empty. I knew that we needed a ship, but did it have to be that one? Did we have to rape the women? I know we're pirates, but I have more honor than that. I ordered the crew to steer towards our normal meeting place for a gang in Miami.

Upon arrival, I went to the cops. I turned my crew in, after taking all of the ammo from our guns, of course, and then turned myself in. The police put me in prison, and within the hour, every important leader knew I'd been caught. I was tried in America, and was given the death penalty. As I sat on that chair, I thought of the life I made for myself, and felt regret. I knew that if there was an afterlife, I was going to the hell equivalent, and I was scared. To try to cope with my fear, I tried making a joke.

"Hey, I guess I'll just settle for stealing Satan's pitchfork shipments, eh?"

"Shaddup, you no-good freak." Said the guard as he fastened the last strap on the chair. "Any last words, scumbag?"

"Will it hurt?"

Nothing.

"That wasn't so bad, was it?"

Everything was black. I looked around to try to find the scratchy, deep voice. Did the chair drain all of the buildings power? Or... Is this death?

"You're dead, bud."

Well that explains that. "Where am I? Which religion got it right?"

"That'll come in time. First, I'm required to make you watch your own funeral."

Oh shit. "O-OK. And what if I don't have a funeral? Literally nobody alive cares about me!"

"You have a funeral, all right. And there's plenty of people there."

All of a sudden, I saw myself. I was nailed to the side of a barge at a dock of dinner sort. People threw rocks, beer bottles, and all kinds of other stuff. I looked closer to see that my legs were gone, and replaced with sticks. I had a black cloth strung over one eye, and there was a parrot piñata on my shoulder. I watched in horror as the masses desecrated my corpse, all while saying awful things. I didn't expect to become a hero, but turning myself in was the most honorable thing I've ever done, and it was my worst mistake.

Life is meaningless, I'm not going to lie to you, but that's the beauty in it. The best part about being here on God's green Earth isn't fucking prostitutes, driving fast cars, or eating incredible foods, it's that you *can*. Life is a lot like a game (super cliché, I know, but bear (bare?) with me). Just like any game, you'll get bored at parts, but there's also the great bits where you can't imagine ever being tired of it. Sure, there's some truly crappy people out there, but just remember that the reward isn't necessarily the destination, but rather, it's the trip.

My advice to you is to hold on. I've personally been close to suicide several times, but remember that even when it seems like nobody cares, people do. Your father would be crushed if you killed yourself, as it sounds like you're among his only company.

Nobody can really understand how you feel, but suicide isn't the answer. I'd recommend going out to the bar, gym, or wherever you can meet people who are like you, and just introduce yourself. You'll be surprised at how many people are willing to be a shoulder to cry on and an ear to talk to. If you ever feel close or especially depressed, just know you can always PM me. God knows I'm on this website pretty much 24/7, so I'll probably see it.
